basis: AlphaDIA's precursor-level directLFQ intensity matrix; normalised when the run sets search_output.normalize_lfq, on by default.
precursor.intensity: AlphaDIA's precursor-level directLFQ intensity; normalised when the run sets search_output.normalize_directlfq, on by default.
pg.intensity: AlphaDIA's protein-group directLFQ intensity; normalised when the run sets search_output.normalize_directlfq, on by default.
ms1_int_sum_apex_dn: AlphaPept's summed MS1 apex intensity after its delayed normalisation, the _dn suffix.
ms1_int_sum_area: summed MS1 peak area, before AlphaPept's delayed normalisation.
Precursor.Quantity: the precursor quantity. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'.

Precursor.Normalised: Precursor.Quantity after cross-run normalisation. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'. Cross-run normalisation is RT-dependent by default, global with --global-norm, and off with --no-norm.

Ms1.Area: the precursor's MS1 peak area, beside its fragment-based quantity; not a Normalised column. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'.

Ms1.Normalised: Ms1.Area after cross-run normalisation; the primary layer of DDA runs. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'. Cross-run normalisation is RT-dependent by default, global with --global-norm, and off with --no-norm.
Fragment.Quant.Raw: DIA-NN's raw fragment quantities at the elution apex, written with --export-quant.
PG.Quantity: the protein-group quantity. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'.

PG.Normalised: PG.Quantity after cross-run normalisation. DIA-NN's output reference: 'Quantity means non-normalised quantity', 'Normalised means normalised quantity'. Cross-run normalisation is RT-dependent by default, global with --global-norm, and off with --no-norm.

PG.MaxLFQ: protein-group quantity by MaxLFQ from the normalised precursors, so it follows the run's normalisation. QuantUMS, since 1.9, changes how the precursors are quantified, not how the protein group is: the protein quantity is still MaxLFQ. Cross-run normalisation is RT-dependent by default, global with --global-norm, and off with --no-norm.
<sample> Intensity in combined_ion.tsv: IonQuant's precursor intensity. IonQuant has a normalisation setting, ionquant.normalization, but whether these columns carry it is not established.
area: MassChroQ's extracted ion chromatogram area per run. Whether the run's settings can normalise this column is not established.
evidence.txt Intensity: the summed extracted ion current of the feature's isotope clusters, never normalised.
modificationSpecificPeptides.txt Intensity <run>: summed peptide intensity, never normalised.
peptides.txt Intensity <run>: summed peptide intensity, never normalised.
peptides.txt LFQ intensity <run>: MaxLFQ, with delayed normalisation unless the run skips it; present only when the run enables LFQ.
proteinGroups.txt Intensity <run>: the protein group's summed peptide intensities, never normalised.
proteinGroups.txt LFQ intensity <run>: MaxLFQ, with delayed normalisation unless the run skips it; present only when the run enables LFQ.
proteinGroups.txt iBAQ <run>: summed intensity divided by the number of theoretically observable peptides, from un-normalised intensities.
Peak intensity in AllQuantifiedPeaks.tsv: FlashLFQ's peak intensity. FlashLFQ has a Normalize setting, but whether this file carries it is not established.

abundance_<sample>: Proline's precursor ion abundance. Proline reports raw_abundance as the extracted ion chromatogram and abundance after its post-processing, which normalises when the run's quantitation settings ask for it.

raw_abundance_<sample>: Proline's raw precursor ion abundance. Proline reports raw_abundance as the extracted ion chromatogram and abundance after its post-processing, which normalises when the run's quantitation settings ask for it.

abundance_<sample> of the Protein sets sheet: Proline's protein-set abundance after its post-processing, which normalises when the run's quantitation settings ask for it. Proline sums or fits a protein set's peptide abundances as the run's quantitation settings choose, which the workbook does not state, so the kind is unknown.

raw_abundance_<sample> of the Protein sets sheet: Proline's raw protein-set abundance. Proline sums or fits a protein set's peptide abundances as the run's quantitation settings choose, which the workbook does not state, so the kind is unknown.
ProteoBench's custom format: intensities the submitter supplies, with no parameter file to say how they were made.
<sample> Normalized Area: the feature area after PEAKS's normalisation; the run's Normalization Method, such as TIC or No Normalization, decides.

abundance_<sample>: Proline's precursor ion abundance. Proline reports raw_abundance as the extracted ion chromatogram and abundance after its post-processing, which normalises when the run's quantitation settings ask for it.
Intensity in msstats_in.csv: OpenMS's feature intensity, before MSstats. Whether the run's settings can normalise this column is not established.
<run> column of lfq.tsv: Sage's MS1 label-free intensity, per precursor charge. Whether the run's settings can normalise this column is not established.
<run> column of lfq.tsv: Sage's MS1 label-free intensity, charge states combined. Whether the run's settings can normalise this column is not established.
FG.Quantity: the precursor quantity at the run's quantity MS level, after cross-run normalisation when the run enables it. The Cross-Run Normalization setting decides; its parameter file states it.
FG.MS2RawQuantity: the precursor's MS2 quantity before normalisation; FG.Quantity's source when the run quantifies on MS2, the default.
FG.MS1RawQuantity: the precursor's MS1 quantity before normalisation.

PG.Quantity: the protein-group quantity from normalised precursor quantities; the run's protein quantity method, such as a top-N mean or MaxLFQ, decides the kind. The Cross-Run Normalization setting decides; its parameter file states it.
F.PeakArea: the fragment's peak area; Spectronaut writes its normalised area as a separate column, F.NormalizedPeakArea.
abundance_<sample>: WOMBAT-P's precursor abundance; the run's normalization_method, such as median, decides its normalisation.
abundance_<sample>: WOMBAT-P's peptidoform abundance; the run's normalization_method, such as median, decides its normalisation.

Observed precursor RT. AlphaDIA output-format documentation specifies seconds for precursor.rt.observed; the 1.12 raw-data wrapper constructs rt_values by multiplying AlphaRaw minute values by 60.
precursor.rt.calibrated is the library RT calibrated into the run: where AlphaDIA expects the precursor, on the run's seconds axis; it differs from RT_Observed by tens of seconds.
The spectral library's RT; the library's own scale, which AlphaDIA calibrates into the run as RT_Calibrated. A layer only because AlphaDIA writes it with run-to-run differences of up to 0.03.
cycle_fwhm, the peak width at half maximum counted in DIA cycles, not time; its duration depends on the cycle time.
precursor.rt.fwhm, 3 for every precursor of a 2.1 submission like cycle_fwhm in 1.12: a count of DIA cycles rather than a time.
rt equals rt_apex, the apex of the feature's MS1 peak in the run. A uniform unit for every supported AlphaPept input route has not been established, so consumers must not assume one.
rt_start, where the feature's MS1 peak begins. A uniform unit for every supported AlphaPept input route has not been established, so consumers must not assume one.
rt_end, where the feature's MS1 peak ends. A uniform unit for every supported AlphaPept input route has not been established, so consumers must not assume one.
fwhm of the feature's MS1 peak, on the same axis as rt. A uniform unit for every supported AlphaPept input route has not been established, so consumers must not assume one.

rt_calib, the apex after AlphaPept aligns the runs for matching between runs; it differs from rt by up to minutes. A uniform unit for every supported AlphaPept input route has not been established, so consumers must not assume one.
Observed precursor retention time in minutes, distinct from library iRT and Predicted.RT.
RT.Start, where the precursor's elution peak begins, in minutes like RT.
RT.Stop, where the precursor's elution peak ends, in minutes like RT.
Estimated peak width at half maximum, in minutes: about 0.06 for RT around 16 in the 2.3 Astral submission.
Predicted.RT, the RT DIA-NN predicts in this run from the library iRT, in minutes.
Predicted.iRT, the observed RT mapped onto the library's iRT scale; it tracks iRT closely.
iRT, the reference RT recorded in the spectral library, the same in every run.

FragPipe output reference defines Apex Retention Time as the retention time of the precursor apex intensity. FragPipe documents the unit as usually seconds but instrument-dependent, so the rule alone does not establish it.
Where the precursor's elution peak begins in the sample. FragPipe documents the unit as usually seconds but instrument-dependent, so the rule alone does not establish it.
Where the precursor's elution peak ends in the sample. FragPipe documents the unit as usually seconds but instrument-dependent, so the rule alone does not establish it.
Width of the precursor's elution peak at half maximum in the sample. FragPipe documents the unit as usually seconds but instrument-dependent, so the rule alone does not establish it.
Evidence Retention time is the uncalibrated retention time in minutes.
Evidence Calibrated retention time is the retention time in minutes after MaxQuant aligns the runs for matching between runs.
Evidence Calibrated retention time start, where the elution peak begins on the calibrated time scale, in minutes.
Evidence Calibrated retention time finish, where the elution peak ends on the calibrated time scale, in minutes.
Evidence Retention length, the total width of the elution peak in minutes.
Modification-specific peptide Retention time is in minutes, averaged over its evidence entries; this is a feature annotation, not a per-run RT measurement.
Modification-specific peptide Calibrated retention time, the calibrated RT in minutes averaged over its evidence entries; a feature annotation.
FlashLFQ's MS2 Retention Time, the scan time of the identifying MS/MS spectrum, in minutes: the committed sample spans 35-131.
FlashLFQ's Peak RT Apex, the apex of the peptide's MS1 peak in the run, in minutes like MS2 Retention Time; - where no peak was found.
FlashLFQ's Peak RT Start, where the MS1 peak begins, in minutes; - where no peak was found.
FlashLFQ's Peak RT End, where the MS1 peak ends, in minutes; - where no peak was found.
Proline's per-run elution_time of the quantified peptide ion. The ProteoBench DDA submission spans 17-135, the range MaxQuant reports in minutes for the same raw files.
Proline's per-run corrected_time, the elution time after map alignment: the runs' values agree within seconds where elution_time differs by minutes.
master_quant_peptide_ion_elution_time, one value per ion within seconds of the median per-run corrected_time.

master_elution_time, one value per ion: within 0.3 min of the earliest run's elution_time and up to minutes from master_quant_peptide_ion_elution_time. Proline does not document which time it is; read as a measured RT.
The per-sample RT mean of the feature, in minutes: the ProteoBench DDA submission spans the range MaxQuant reports in minutes for the same raw files.
The feature's RT mean across samples, in minutes like the per-sample values; a feature annotation.
Proline's per-run elution_time of the quantified peptide ion. The ProteoBench DDA submission spans 17-135, the range MaxQuant reports in minutes for the same raw files.
Proline's per-run corrected_time, the elution time after map alignment: the runs' values agree within seconds where elution_time differs by minutes.
master_quant_peptide_ion_elution_time, one value per ion within seconds of the median per-run corrected_time.

master_elution_time, one value per ion: within 0.3 min of the earliest run's elution_time and up to minutes from master_quant_peptide_ion_elution_time. Proline does not document which time it is; read as a measured RT.

EG.ApexRT, the apex of the precursor's elution peak in the run. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.

EG.StartRT, where the elution peak begins; it precedes EG.ApexRT in all but 0.01% of rows. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.

EG.EndRT, where the elution peak ends; it follows EG.ApexRT. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.

EG.FWHM, the peak width at half maximum on the RT axis; EG.FWHM (iRT) is the iRT-scale twin. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.

EG.PeakWidth, the full width of the elution peak, wider than EG.FWHM. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.

EG.RTPredicted, the library iRT calibrated into the run: where Spectronaut expects the precursor. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.
EG.iRTEmpirical, the observed apex converted to the iRT scale; it tracks EG.iRTPredicted.
EG.StartiRT, the peak start on the iRT scale. It brackets EG.iRTEmpirical in only a quarter of the rows of a 240-minute report, so its relation to the apex is not established.
EG.EndiRT, the peak end on the iRT scale; see EG_StartiRT for the open question.
EG.FWHM (iRT), the width at half maximum on the iRT scale.

EG.MeanApexRT differs between runs for one precursor and equals EG.ApexRT in most rows, so it is not an experiment-wide mean; what it averages over is not documented. Spectronaut reports EG retention times in minutes: EG.ApexRT lies around 14 in a ProteoBench 15-minute Astral submission and reaches 249 in a 240-minute run.
EG.iRTPredicted, the library iRT of the precursor, the same in every run.
